question: 5 men and 3 women can earn ₹8,400 in 4 days. 9 men and 7 women can earn ₹28,700 in 7 days. In how many days will 8 men and 5 women earn ₹30,600?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
1 day earning of 5M + 3W = 8400 ÷ 4 = ₹2100 ... (i)

1 day earning of 9M + 7W = 28700 ÷ 7 = ₹4100 ... (ii)

Solve (i) × 7 − (ii) × 3: (35M + 21W) − (27M + 21W) = 14700 − 12300

8M = 2400 ⇒ M = ₹300, and substituting M gives W = ₹200.

Daily earning of 8M + 5W = 8(300) + 5(200) = ₹3400.

Total days to earn ₹30600 = 30600 ÷ 3400 = 9 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Earning of 5 men and 3 women in 4 days = ₹8,400

Earning of 9 men and 7 women in 7 days = ₹28,700

**Calculations:**

Let the daily earning of 1 man be M and 1 woman be W.

⇒ (5M + 3W) × 4 = 8400

⇒ 5M + 3W = 2100 ---- (Equation 1)

⇒ (9M + 7W) × 7 = 28700

⇒ 9M + 7W = 4100 ---- (Equation 2)

Multiplying Equation 1 by 7 and Equation 2 by 3:

⇒ 35M + 21W = 14700 ---- (Equation 3)

⇒ 27M + 21W = 12300 ---- (Equation 4)

Subtracting Equation 4 from Equation 3:

⇒ 35M − 27M = 14700 − 12300

⇒ 8M = 2400

⇒ M = 300

Substitute M = 300 in Equation 1:

⇒ 5(300) + 3W = 2100

⇒ 1500 + 3W = 2100

⇒ 3W = 600

⇒ W = 200

Calculate the daily earning of 8 men and 5 women:

⇒ 8M + 5W = 8(300) + 5(200)

⇒ Total daily earning = 2400 + 1000 = ₹3400

Number of days required to earn ₹30,600:

⇒ Required Days = Total Target Earning ÷ Daily Earning

⇒ Required Days = 30600 ÷ 3400 = 9 days

**∴ The correct answer is 9 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work & Wages Rule

Wages are distributed in direct proportion to the work done by individuals. When individuals work for the same number of days, their total wages are shared in the ratio of their daily efficiencies or one-day earnings.

Simultaneous Linear Equations

For a system of two variables, equations can be solved by scaling one or both equations to equalize the coefficients of one variable, then adding or subtracting to eliminate it and solve for the remaining unknown.

Unitary Method Application

The fastest way to equate different groups working for different time periods is to calculate the earnings or work done for exactly 1 unit of time (1 day) to establish a common proportional base.
